title: originSpiral tone-by-omission below the plot floor (F-10, third pass) — review + orchestrator follow-up
REVISION_NOTE: This report.json was REWRITTEN after review (docs/3d-audit/lane-reports/W-10c-review.md, ACCEPT-WITH-FOLLOWUPS) and a subsequent orchestrator visual re-check found the torus wedge is NOT fixed. The original `before` array pointed at `after/W-10/shots/B/*`, which review discovered is byte-identical to `after/W-10c` (a stale/corrupted historical folder, not a genuine 78bbf3e8 capture). `before` now points at freshly re-captured 78bbf3e8 output under `after/W-10c/before-78bbf3e8/` (all 12 md5s independently verified to differ from their `after` counterpart — see `byte_identical_pairs`). The `looked_at_images`/`notes` fields below also REPLACE the original overly-positive characterization with a corrected, quantified finding: the torus wedge is real, unfixed, and by one honest measure slightly WORSE after 441af81f, not better.
notes: Third pass on F-10 (after W-10 0.5x-pen and W-10b 0.8x-pen, both DONE/FU with 10-12% of torus/cone ring-to-ring gaps still under 1.0x pen and the orchestrator's eye reading the torus lower-left fan as solid white wedges). W-10c raises the floor to the FULL 1.0x pen (drawn rings never sit closer than one pen width) and attempts to buy the lost tone back a different way: where the tone-driven pitch asks for less than the floor, `localDuty = round(floor / wanted)` (capped at 4) is computed per-angle, and the arc where duty >= L is retraced as its own separate emitScr pass, L-1 additional times, AT THE SAME RADIUS as the ring just drawn. CORRECTED FINDING (this revision): retracing the identical curve at the identical radius adds essentially ZERO new screen coverage — confirmed by disabling the retrace loop in a scratch copy and rendering the same torus cell: pixel diff vs retrace-enabled was only 2129/320000 px (0.67%), all faint antialiasing jitter, no meaningful new ink. The 5-8% 'ink length' increase measured in the original pass was real but illusory as a coverage metric: it counts duplicate strokes covering already-inked pixels, not new dark area. Net effect on the torus wedge: raising the floor from 0.8x to 1.0x pen mechanically WIDENS the true ring-to-ring gap wherever the floor was already engaging (by definition, +25% wider at every affected angle), and the retrace mechanism cannot compensate for that widening because it never draws a new, different-radius ring. Directly measured (run-length analysis on the rendered PNGs, interior band x:100-400,y:295-325, pen width calibrated at 7px from an unambiguous tight-ring region): fraction of that band's pixels sitting in a continuous blank-paper run > 2 pen-widths went from 73.9% (78bbf3e8) to 87.8% (441af81f) — WORSE, not better. The identical measurement on cone (interior band x:150-400,y:290-320, pen calibrated at 2px) moved only 67.2% -> 67.6% — within noise, matching the orchestrator's visual read that cone is unaffected. Root cause is structural, not a tuning gap: a 1-pen-minimum floor and a 'no gap wider than ~2 pens' visual bar are in direct tension wherever the local wanted tone pitch is intrinsically sparser than 2x the floor — no compensation mechanism that only re-draws EXISTING rings (rather than inserting a genuinely new, closer-but-still->=1-pen ring, which is only possible where duty was already 1) can close that gap. A real fix would need either a different fill strategy for torus specifically, or accepting the floor-driven sparsity there as an intended limit of this law.

A prior draft of this guard read the internal __spiralDuty trace instead and was PROVEN not mutation-sensitive (all values there are computed before the retrace loop runs, so disabling that loop left the trace-based test green) -- corrected in this revision; the trace-based test is kept as a separate, honestly-scoped 'duty is computed correctly' check, not a retrace-emission guard.
tests.duty_cap_boundary: New test verifies duty === clamp(dutyRaw, 1, 4) for every recorded sample (correctness of the clamp itself). Honest finding: DUTY_CAP=4 does not actually engage on any tested fixture -- torus max observed dutyRaw is 3, and forcing penWidth to 3x the default (0.9 vs 0.3, to inflate PLOT_MIN_PEN/wanted) still topped out at 3 (pitchFor's own floor INK/A_DARK scales with the same inkWidth/penWidth pair that sets PLOT_MIN_PEN, so the ratio stays roughly fixed regardless of absolute pen size -- a structural reason, not a fixture accident). Recorded rather than asserted as 'engages'.

The retrace mechanism is confirmed active (mutation-tested) and safe (0% of gaps under 1.0x pen either before OR after this specific check, since W-10b already cleared the OLD 0.8x bar and W-10c's own bar is 1.0x), but it is NOT the fix for the user-visible wedge: retracing an existing ring cannot add new coverage between two ADJACENT rings that the floor raise pushed further apart. Cone (cone__hatch__originSpiral__med__a, and max, byte-identical): visually near-identical pre/post, confirmed quantitatively (67.2% -> 67.6% in the same run-length metric, within noise) -- the orchestrator's read that cone is fine is confirmed. Sphere: visually identical pre/post, clean evenly-spaced spiral, no defect, confirmed by the existing tonal-range/wrap-foreshorten tests plus the +2.2% ink delta (well inside tolerance).

orchestrator_followup_response.item_1_explain_discrepancy: DONE -- see `notes` above. Mechanism: floor raise (0.8x->1.0x pen) widens real ring-to-ring gaps wherever the floor engages; retrace re-draws the SAME already-inked ring (confirmed near-zero pixel effect, 0.67% diff, when disabled vs enabled) so it cannot fill the widened gap. Quantified: torus interior-band blank-run->2pen fraction 73.9%->87.8% (worse); cone 67.2%->67.6% (unaffected, matches orchestrator's visual read). The geometry making the wedge is simply the widened floor-clamped radial step itself -- NOT an off-surface/hole-crossing spoke artifact (that hypothesis was tested and disproven: cone has an almost identical ~41% permanently-off-surface angular sector from the highlight origin as torus does, 40.8% vs 41.1%, yet cone shows no wedge -- so the dead-zone fraction alone does not explain the torus-specific defect; the floor-widening mechanism above does, and is directly measured on the rendered pixels).
orchestrator_followup_response.item_2_real_fix_in_2h: NOT ACHIEVABLE, and not attempted as a code change for this reason: any compensation that only re-draws already-existing rings (retrace, as shipped) cannot add coverage between two rings the floor has pushed apart; the only way to add real coverage is a genuinely NEW, offset ring, which by construction would need to sit closer than the current ring by less than 1 full pen wherever `wanted < floor` -- i.e. it would reintroduce the exact sub-floor crowding W-10/W-10b/W-10c exist to eliminate. This is a proven structural tension (1-pen-minimum floor vs 'no visual gap over ~2 pens' bar in the same low-tone region), not a missing parameter. A genuinely different fill strategy for torus (not explored here, out of scope for this budget) would be required.
orchestrator_followup_response.item_3_hide_via_isReachableOn: SPEC READY, NOT IMPLEMENTED -- BLOCKED BY LANE FILE SERIALIZATION. `SCENE_FILL_STYLES.isReachableOn` lives in `src/config/context-bar.js`, which `docs/3d-audit/lane-reports/AGENT-PROTOCOL.md`'s file-serialization table assigns to the `fill-audit` lane, not `fill-audit-c` (this lane's exclusive file is `surface-fill-mono.js`). Editing it here would cross a hard protocol boundary and risk colliding with that lane's own live concurrent session (confirmed active this session: docs/3d-audit/STILL-OPEN.md was modified by the fill-audit lane's W-15c work while this unit was in progress). Exact patch for whoever owns that file: add, inside `SCENE_FILL_STYLES.isReachableOn` (src/config/context-bar.js, in the curved/chart-wrapped branch, after the spiral/stipple and pyramid+hatch+fineLadder checks, before the final `return true;`): `if (primitiveMode === 'torus' && id === 'originSpiral') return false;` -- plus a picker test (likely `tests/unit/scene3d-fill-style-picker.test.js` or similar, also outside this lane) asserting the Fill Style row for originSpiral disappears when primitiveMode is torus and remains present for cone and sphere. Cone and sphere are NOT affected by this defect (see measurements above) and should keep the current 1.0x-floor + retrace behavior as-is.

iteration_3.ruling: Since the torus wedge fraction got WORSE (73.9% -> 87.8%), the orchestrator ruled torus must not ship the iteration-2 mechanism at all: gate floor-raise+retrace off for torus (byte-identical to 78bbf3e8/W-10b) while cone/sphere keep iteration 2, prove it with md5, add a test pinning the gate, and record the W-10b wedge number as the honest open metric.
iteration_3.honest_open_number_W10b_wedge_fraction: 73.9% -- the fraction of the measured torus interior band (x:100-400, y:295-325 in the 800x400 render, pen calibrated at 7px) sitting in a continuous blank-paper run over 2 pen widths, AT 78bbf3e8/W-10b (0.8x-pen floor, no retrace). This is the number the torus SHOULD revert to if gated; iteration 2 (441af81f/04ab79bd) measured 87.8% on the same band -- worse. Recorded here per the ruling as the still-open, unresolved defect: even W-10b's own 73.9% is a large majority of the band reading as blank paper -- gating back to it stops the regression but does not fix the underlying wedge.
iteration_3.gate_NOT_shipped_why: A code-level gate could not be implemented reliably from within this lane's file (surface-fill-mono.js) and was NOT shipped -- see commit e6b85de4 and the new test describe block 'W-10c iteration 3 -- hole-detection reliability' in scene3d-origin-spiral-tonal-range.test.js for the full investigation. Two blockers, both confirmed by direct measurement, not assumption: (1) NO PRIMITIVE IDENTITY reaches this file -- the opts bag `Vectura.Scene3D.SurfaceFillMono.emit()` receives from `surface-fill.js`'s `MonoFill().emit({...})` call site (~line 10202) carries no mode/primitive/shape field at all; `chartFor(opts.mode, opts.sizes)` (surface-fill.js ~line 176) resolves the primitive to a bare parametrisation function before this file ever sees it -- there is no string/tag to branch on. (2) A GEOMETRIC/topological stand-in (flood-fill hole detection: does the silhouette enclose an off-surface region, sampled purely through C.inv, independent of any opts field) was implemented and tested and is PROVEN UNRELIABLE on the exact scene that matters: on an off-axis test camera it works perfectly (torus ~40% enclosed area at grid sizes 24-64, cone/sphere exactly 0%, every trial) but on the real default-camera gallery scene (the one the wedge screenshots and the mutation guard both use) it measures 0% enclosed area at grid sizes 24/32/48/64/128/160 and a single spurious 0.02%-area 2-cell 'hole' at grid size 96 only -- indistinguishable from grid-alignment aliasing, not a real hole. A signal that flickers on at one arbitrary resolution and off at every neighbour, on the exact scene needing protection, cannot back a byte-identity-critical gate; shipping it would have been cosmetic (verified: implementing it anyway and running it against the real gallery scene left torus UNCHANGED from iteration 2 -- 409 paths / 1551.7mm ink, identical to no-gate -- because the detector correctly said 'no hole' there). Implemented, verified broken, and REVERTED before commit rather than shipped.
